sources.title: UK GDPR Article 5
sources.taken: processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner in relation to the data subject (‘lawfulness, fairness and transparency’)
sources.also_taken: adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed (‘data minimisation’)
sources.note: Article 5(1)(a) and Article 5(1)(c) were read on 17 November 2026. Article 5(1)(b) and Article 5(1)(e) were not copied. Article 6 and Article 9 were not opened. A lawful basis is not asserted.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 22A
sources.taken: a decision is based solely on automated processing if there is no meaningful human involvement in the taking of the decision, and a decision is a significant decision, in relation to a data subject, if it produces a legal effect for the data subject, or it has a similarly significant effect for the data subject
sources.note: UK GDPR Article 22A, as published on legislation.gov.uk on 17 November 2026, is annotated as substituted for Article 22 on 19 June 2025 for specified purposes and on 5 February 2026 in so far as not already in force, by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 sections 80(1) and 142(1) and (2)(h), and by S.I. 2026/82 regulation 2(j), with regulation 5. The same footnote is on Articles 22B, 22C, and 22D. Regulation 5 was not opened and is not interpreted. Article 22B(2) was not in the text returned for Article 22B and is not quoted. No regulations under Article 22D were read. Whether any have been made was not checked and is unverified.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 22B
sources.taken: A significant decision based entirely or partly on processing described in Article 9(1) (processing of special categories of personal data) may not be taken based solely on automated processing, unless one of the following conditions is met.
sources.note: Article 22B(1), Article 22B(3), and Article 22B(4) were in the text returned on 17 November 2026. Article 22B(2) was not in that text and is not quoted. Article 22B(4) refers to Article 6(1)(ea). Article 6 was not opened. This starter does not decide that a condition is met.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 22C
sources.taken: The safeguards must consist of or include measures which provide the data subject with information about decisions described in paragraph 1 taken in relation to the data subject, enable the data subject to make representations about such decisions, enable the data subject to obtain human intervention on the part of the controller in relation to such decisions, and enable the data subject to contest such decisions.
sources.note: Article 22C(1) and Article 22C(2) were read. Article 22C(1) refers to regulations under Article 22D(3). Those regulations were not read.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 22D
sources.taken: The Secretary of State may by regulations provide that, for the purposes of Article 22A(1)(a), there is, or is not, to be taken to be meaningful human involvement in the taking of a decision in cases described in the regulations.
sources.note: Article 22D(1) to (5) were read. Article 22D(4) says regulations under paragraph 3 may not amend Article 22C. Article 22D(5) says regulations under this Article are subject to the affirmative resolution procedure. No such regulations were read. Whether any have been made is unverified.

sources.title: Equality Act 2010, section 4
sources.taken: The following characteristics are protected characteristics— age; disability; gender reassignment; marriage and civil partnership; pregnancy and maternity; race; religion or belief; sex; sexual orientation.
sources.note: The page said section 4 is up to date with all changes known to be in force on or before 16 November 2026. Extent England and Wales and Scotland. The listed characteristics are not inferred about a person. Northern Ireland equality law was not opened.

sources.title: Equality Act 2010, section 39
sources.taken: An employer (A) must not discriminate against an employee of A's (B)— as to B's terms of employment; in the way A affords B access, or by not affording B access, to opportunities for promotion, transfer or training or for receiving any other benefit, facility or service; by dismissing B; by subjecting B to any other detriment.
sources.note: The page said section 39 is up to date with all changes known to be in force on or before 17 November 2026. Section 39(2) prohibits discrimination against an employee. Section 39(5) says a duty to make reasonable adjustments applies to an employer. This starter does not decide that either has been met or breached. Extent England and Wales and Scotland.

sources.title: Employment practices and data protection: monitoring workers
sources.note: The hub says the guidance is under review because of the Data (Use and Access) Act and may change. It says the guidance helps employers comply with the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. This starter does not decide that preparing a one-to-one from sources a manager selected is monitoring, and it does not decide that monitoring is lawful.

sources.title: What do we need to do if we use monitoring tools that use solely automated processes?
sources.note: The ICO page 'What do we need to do if we use monitoring tools that use solely automated processes?' still names Article 22 of the UK GDPR. It says a similarly significant effect is likely to include a decision that significantly affects someone's financial circumstance, for example increasing or decreasing a worker's pay based on their performance at work, or that affects a worker's employment opportunities, for example dismissing someone. It says human oversight should not be a token gesture. The page carries a banner that the guidance is under review because of the Data (Use and Access) Act and may change. This starter has not reconciled that page with Articles 22A to 22D. That reconciliation is unverified.

sources.title: Harnesses in Copilot Studio
sources.note: Opened on 17 November 2026. The page names the Microsoft Copilot harness, the Customer Conversation harness, and the standard harness. It describes the Microsoft Copilot harness as a runtime for reasoning-heavy multi-step work, with skills, memory, file creation, and a sandbox, billed in Copilot Credits. It does not use the words GitHub Copilot harness. A price was not on the page. Any price is unverified. This starter does not call Copilot Studio.
